hyps.sol: publish a single, dated, version-controlled document checklist with annotated samples and change alerts
hyps.ben: fewer students will arrive missing a document
hyps.why: they can confirm every item against an authoritative source before travel
hyps.metric: day-of-registration document exceptions fall by at least 50% compared with the 2026 cycle, and at least 85% of pilot users list every required document correctly in a comprehension test
hyps.assume: The admissions office can freeze requirements at least 10 days before reporting
hyps.test: Comprehension test with 15 to 20 current first years using a paper prototype; exception log next cycle
hyps.fail: Below 70% comprehension, or exceptions fall by less than 25%

hyps.sol: show a per-document status (Uploaded, Under review, Accepted, Action needed) and a downloadable readiness receipt
hyps.user: students completing ERP steps from home
hyps.ben: they will resolve digital issues before travelling
hyps.why: they can see exactly what is still pending instead of guessing
hyps.metric: at least 80% of students reach “Ready” status 48 hours or more before reporting, and campus upload-desk visits drop by 60%
hyps.assume: Verification staff can review uploads within 48 hours
hyps.test: Clickable Figma prototype tested with 10 students; staff time-and-motion estimate

hyps.sol: give each arriving student a digital token that shows their full desk route and a live estimated wait
hyps.user: first years and families on reporting day
hyps.ben: they will feel less lost and ask fewer “where next?” questions
hyps.why: the sequence and the wait become visible instead of unknown
hyps.metric: wayfinding questions at help points fall by 50%, and at least 70% of surveyed students rate the on-campus step 4 out of 5 or higher for clarity
hyps.assume: Desk throughput is stable enough to estimate waits
hyps.test: Role-play simulation of the hall with 3 desks, printed route cards and a volunteer timer

hyps.sol: run an official help channel staffed by trained senior volunteers who work from one verified FAQ
hyps.user: newcomers who currently rely on unofficial WhatsApp groups
hyps.ben: they will choose the official channel for answers
hyps.why: it combines a senior’s speed and tone with official accuracy
hyps.metric: median first reply is under 10 minutes during reporting week, at least 60% of first years ask at least one question there, and reports of conflicting answers fall
hyps.assume: Seniors will volunteer, and the office will keep the FAQ current
hyps.test: Wizard-of-Oz pilot: 4 volunteers answer questions from one batch section for a week
hyps.fail: Median reply over 30 minutes, or under 30% adoption

hyps.sol: require every room to pass a pre-handover inspection and put a scan-to-report defect code on each door

hyps.test: Inspect a sample of 20 rooms with the checklist; trial the QR form in one wing

scamper.before: A push-button on poles that sounds a bell and lights a “STOP” sign. It is hard to reach in a crowd, out of reach for some wheelchair users and children, and gives no confirmation to the person who pressed it.

rows.name: Substitute
rows.idea: Replace the push-button with a capacitive touch strip along every handrail, reachable from any seat or standing spot.
rows.why: Accessibility and hygiene; nobody has to push through a crowd

rows.name: Combine
rows.idea: Merge stop request with assistance and SOS: short press to stop, long press for “need ramp or more time”, triple press for a silent alert to the driver and control room.
rows.why: Safety and accessibility from one familiar control

rows.name: Adapt
rows.idea: Borrow from the aircraft cabin call bell and game-controller haptics: the strip glows, vibrates to confirm, and shows the seat zone on the driver display.
rows.why: The person pressing knows the request was received

rows.name: Modify / Magnify
rows.idea: Enlarge the feedback: a large LED panel reads “STOP REQUESTED · Next: Civil Lines · ramp needed”, with an audio confirmation.
rows.why: Visually and hearing-impaired passengers are both informed

rows.name: Put to another use
rows.idea: Off-peak, the strip becomes a one-press poll (“Was this bus clean?”), feeding the operator dashboard.
rows.why: Engagement; continuous service-quality data

rows.name: Eliminate
rows.idea: Remove the button entirely: the destination on the digital ticket or NCMC tap registers the stop automatically.
rows.why: No action needed from passengers; fewer missed stops

rows.name: Reverse / Rearrange
rows.idea: Reverse who signals: the bus tells the passenger. The ticket or phone vibrates “your stop is next” one stop ahead.
rows.why: Removes anxiety about missing the stop, especially for newcomers

scamper.before: A static PDF on the website listing documents for all categories. It has no version date and no samples, and it does not show which items the student has already completed. In A1, students reported documents asked for on campus that were not in this list.

rows.name: Substitute
rows.idea: Replace the static PDF with a personalised interactive checklist generated from the student’s JoSAA category, state and quota.
rows.why: Each student sees only their own items, which cuts confusion (US-01)

rows.name: Combine
rows.idea: Merge the checklist with the ERP upload: each checklist line is its own upload slot with a status light (grey, amber, green, red).
rows.why: One place for “what” and “done”; addresses the missing accepted status (H2)

rows.name: Adapt
rows.idea: Borrow airline web check-in: when every item turns green, issue a “Ready to Report” boarding pass with QR and reporting slot.
rows.why: Tangible proof before travel for student and parents (H1, H2)

rows.name: Modify / Magnify
rows.idea: Magnify the examples: an annotated sample for every document showing where the stamp, signature and date must go.
rows.why: Fewer rejected or wrongly notarised documents (US-02)

rows.name: Put to another use
rows.idea: After admissions, the same checklist becomes the official FAQ knowledge base for senior volunteers and the WhatsApp bot.
rows.why: One source of truth for every helper (US-19, H4)

rows.name: Eliminate
rows.idea: Drop documents already verified through JoSAA or DigiLocker, and drop notarisation wherever institute policy accepts self-attestation.
rows.why: Shorter list, less cost, fewer notary visits (US-04)

rows.name: Reverse / Rearrange
rows.idea: Reverse the burden: the institute pre-fills what it already knows (“we have 7 of 9; upload these 2”) instead of the student discovering requirements.
rows.why: The institute proves readiness to the student (HMW H06)

scamper.feature: Paper token queue at the registration hall
scamper.before: A paper slip with a number, issued at the entrance. It does not show which desk comes next or how long the wait is. Tokens ran out for later arrivals, and families waited standing in the heat (A1: QUE ≈9, NAV ≈8).

rows.name: Substitute
rows.idea: Replace paper with a QR e-token on SMS or WhatsApp, tied to a pre-assigned reporting slot.
rows.why: No running out of tokens; arrival is spread through the day (US-16)

rows.name: Combine
rows.idea: Merge the token with the personal desk route and hostel room number: one pass for the whole day.
rows.why: Students always know the next step (US-13, H3)

rows.name: Adapt
rows.idea: Borrow theme-park virtual queues and hospital OPD displays: families wait anywhere and are pinged when their desk is near.
rows.why: Families can rest in shade instead of standing in line

rows.name: Modify / Magnify
rows.idea: Magnify visibility: big now-serving screens per desk with average time per student and the live total wait.
rows.why: The wait becomes known and plannable (US-14)

rows.name: Put to another use
rows.idea: Off-peak, token kiosks and screens become hostel defect-ticket desks and orientation schedule boards.
rows.why: Reuses the hardware; supports room readiness (H5)

rows.name: Eliminate
rows.idea: Remove the queue for pre-verified students: a green express lane straight to ID photo and hostel.
rows.why: Rewards pre-arrival work; shortens queues for everyone

rows.name: Reverse / Rearrange
